Hi Emma — quick technical clarification on how the billing math works for classifier / rerank workloads:

- Metering unit: "scored-item" (we charge per candidate that the model processes). For each scored-item we count the tokens consumed during the forward pass; the unit price we quote is effectively per-scored-item normalized to an average token profile.
- Overhead charge: a small per-request routing fee (applies when you make many micro-calls rather than batched calls). This is why batching yields large savings.
- Batching/caching: If you send a batch of N candidates in a single API call, we still bill N scored-items; however batching reduces compute overhead (lower per-item effective cost) and may allow more efficient kernel selection.
- Short-circuit / cheap reprieves: If you use our prefix-KV cache (when candidates share long prefixes), we can avoid repeated computation on identical tokens — metering still counts what executes on the runtime; we document common cache-hit scenarios in the attached pilot ratecard.
- Peak handling: For burst windows, our autoscale incurs additional short-term compute but billing remains per-scored-item; you can cap burst capacity via routing policies to control costs.

I'll attach a worked example for your numbers: 50M monthly calls x avg 20 candidates -> 1B scored-items. Then show typical per-1k unit costs across bands.

--Marissa
